title: Taming the Factor Zoo: A Test of New Factors
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; methodology; empirical analysis; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines the contribution of a new factor as incremental pricing content relative to a high-dimensional benchmark and keeps SDF loadings distinct from risk-premium estimates.
transfer_limit: Double-selection LASSO assumptions and a 150-factor library are problem-specific; do not impose this procedure on a low-dimensional factor paper.

title: Duration-Driven Returns
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; cash-flow timing; dividend-futures tests; factor regressions; conclusion
teaching_function: Compresses several major factors into a common economic attribute and then tests that explanation using cash flows at different maturities rather than another correlated sort.
transfer_limit: Single-stock dividend futures are unusually informative; ordinary equity sorts alone cannot support the same duration interpretation.

title: Measuring “Dark Matter” in Asset Pricing Models
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; motivating example; formal measure; quantitative examples; out-of-sample implications; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from an intuitive model-fragility problem to a formal diagnostic and then demonstrates what the diagnostic changes in familiar structural models.
transfer_limit: The cosmology analogy cannot substitute for the formal information restrictions; applications require structural-model and specification-test expertise.

title: Model-Free International Stochastic Discount Factors
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; theoretical framework; market-structure comparison; SDF decomposition; empirical analysis; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses alternative market structures to organize theory and empirics around exactly which SDF and exchange-rate relations survive integration or segmentation.
transfer_limit: Minimum-dispersion SDFs are analytical objects rather than direct measures of marginal utility; segmentation assumptions must remain explicit.

title: Asset Managers: Institutional Performance and Factor Exposures
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; data; benchmark ladder; gross and net performance; factor exposures; conclusion
teaching_function: States performance in basis points and moves through strategy benchmarks, fees, factor exposure and feasible institutional alternatives before interpreting skill.
transfer_limit: The proprietary institutional-account sample and 2000–2012 period do not justify claims about all managers or retail mutual funds.

title: Luck versus Skill in the Cross Section of Mutual Fund Returns: Reexamining the Evidence
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; method comparison; size-and-power simulations; empirical reconciliation; conclusion
teaching_function: Turns conflicting published conclusions into a precise comparison of sample construction, bootstrap design, test size and power.
transfer_limit: The reconciliation is bootstrap- and sample-specific; it is not a general license to label extreme fund returns as skill.

title: What Drives Anomaly Returns?
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; return decomposition; anomaly evidence; overfitting checks; interpretation; conclusion
teaching_function: Reorganizes anomaly evidence around cash-flow and discount-rate news and uses the same decomposition across individual anomalies and their efficient combination.
transfer_limit: VAR news components are model-dependent and evidence from five anomalies should not be presented as a universal decomposition of the factor zoo.

title: Anomalies and Their Short-Sale Costs
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; anomaly and borrow-fee data; gross returns; high-fee exclusions; fee-adjusted returns; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds an implementation funnel from published anomaly returns to feasible short positions and net returns while keeping the short leg visible.
transfer_limit: Borrow fees and lending availability vary by investor and period; the estimates do not prove that every anomaly is untradeable for every institution.

title: Test Assets and Weak Factors
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; methodology; simulations; empirical analysis; model diagnosis; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows that weak-factor inference and test-asset choice are one problem and makes the diagnostic role of the selected cross-section part of the main claim.
transfer_limit: The SPCA solution is technically specialized and does not supply a universally optimal set of test assets.

title: The Banking View of Bond Risk Premia
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; state-variable construction; real-time return forecasts; benchmark comparisons; interpretation challenges; conclusion
teaching_function: Introduces an intermediary balance-sheet object missing from standard bond-premium work and tests forecasting power before discussing equilibrium interpretation.
transfer_limit: Forecasting Treasury returns with bank exposure does not alone identify a causal bank-balance-sheet pricing channel.

title: Late to Recessions: Stocks and the Business Cycle
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; stylized facts; real-time state-space framework; strategy evidence; mechanism evidence; conclusion
teaching_function: Begins with a state-dependent return pattern and then separates real-time recession measurement, portfolio consequences and a possible expectations mechanism.
transfer_limit: The number of recession episodes is limited and conclusions depend on real-time state classification rather than revised macroeconomic dates.

title: Volatility Expectations and Returns
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; survey evidence; option-price evidence; model; calibration; alternative explanations; conclusion
teaching_function: Triangulates a belief mechanism with surveys, volatility-linked claims and a calibrated model instead of treating a fitted model as mechanism evidence by itself.
transfer_limit: The representative-agent calibration and extrapolative-belief specification are not separately identified by every matched moment.

title: A Horizon-Based Decomposition of Mutual Fund Value Added Using Transactions
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; motivating model; transaction decomposition; horizon results; trading costs; conclusion
teaching_function: Lets the economic horizon determine the performance decomposition and connects turnover, price impact and announcement-day value added.
transfer_limit: The transaction data and horizon-specific value-added measure are unusual; announcement concentration should not be generalized to other fund populations.

title: Segmented Arbitrage
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; motivating model; factor structure of spreads; funding evidence; balance-sheet evidence; discussion
teaching_function: Uses the low comovement of 32 arbitrage spreads to reject a representative-intermediary benchmark and then brings in quantity data to distinguish two forms of segmentation.
transfer_limit: Spread correlations alone do not identify funding versus balance-sheet segmentation and some apparent arbitrages retain operational risk.
metadata_note: The MinerU conclusion heading is incompletely recovered; use the discussion-and-conclusion content rather than the heading token.

title: Forest through the Trees: Building Cross-Sections of Stock Returns
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; test-asset objective; tree construction; pruning; empirical design; out-of-sample tests; conclusion
teaching_function: Frames trees as a way to construct informative and interpretable test assets rather than as a generic forecasting contest and evaluates spanning out of sample.
transfer_limit: Tree splits and pruning depend on the characteristic universe; the procedure is not a drop-in replacement for a paper whose object is pure return prediction.

title: Anomaly Time
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; information-processing predictions; release-date data; timing results; implementation guidance; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes information availability part of the economic fact and distinguishes stale signals from look-ahead bias before recommending portfolio timing.
transfer_limit: Compustat Snapshot mainly disciplines accounting signals; the same release convention need not apply to market or alternative data.

title: Asset Pricing: A Tale of Night and Day
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data and methodology; session decomposition; portfolio and stock tests; mechanisms; conclusion
teaching_function: Resolves a weak full-day CAPM relation by decomposing returns at an economically meaningful market boundary and repeating the contrast across assets and countries.
transfer_limit: Overnight and intraday returns have distinct microstructure and institutional features; the result is not a general vindication of the CAPM.
metadata_note: MinerU retains a Journal Pre-proof label; DOI and year come from the strict final-publication inventory.

title: Anomalies across the globe: Once public, no longer existent?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; anomaly construction; pre/post-sample tests; pre/post-publication tests; cross-country comparison; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a large international design to distinguish post-publication decay, post-sample decay and cross-market arbitrage barriers rather than reporting another anomaly average.
transfer_limit: Publication dates, database quality and feasible trading differ across countries; non-US persistence is not by itself proof of mispricing.
metadata_note: MinerU retains an Accepted Manuscript label; canonical publication year is 2020.

title: The conditional expected market return
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; theoretical bounds; option-based construction; empirical tightness; term structure; conclusion
teaching_function: Begins with an economically central unobservable object and derives real-time upper and lower bounds before reporting their tightness and magnitude.
transfer_limit: The estimates remain bounds under no-arbitrage and preference restrictions; they should not be described as directly observed expected returns.
metadata_note: MinerU retains a Journal Pre-proof label.

title: What you see is not what you get: The costs of trading market anomalies
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; related literature; implementation-cost estimator; mutual-fund evidence; factor comparisons; conclusion
teaching_function: Turns the paper-versus-practice question into an all-in implementation-cost estimand and reports how costs differ across factors.
transfer_limit: Manager-return exposures deliver aggregate implementation estimates rather than the cost schedule of a particular optimal trade.
metadata_note: MinerU retains a Journal Pre-proof label.

title: Why do discount rates vary?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; motivating moment; methodology; stock and bond evidence; model discrimination; conclusion
teaching_function: Narrows a broad theoretical dispute to the sign of the price of discount-rate risk and explains why that moment discriminates among mechanisms.
transfer_limit: One diagnostic moment narrows models but cannot identify a complete preference, technology or belief mechanism.
metadata_note: MinerU retains a Journal Pre-proof label.

title: Spectral factor models
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; intuition; formal factor structure; identification; empirical application; conclusion
teaching_function: Introduces frequency-specific factors first through economic intuition and only then through formal representation, identification and pricing tests.
transfer_limit: Spectral components are statistical cycles rather than automatically interpretable economic shocks.

title: Estimating the anomaly base rate
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; seminar thought experiment; inference problem; simulations; anomaly estimates; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes the latent universe of unsuccessful research attempts explicit and connects a familiar single test to the posterior probability that an anomaly is real.
transfer_limit: The estimated base rate depends on a model of the unobserved research universe and should not become a universal prior for every signal family.

title: Market efficiency and limits to arbitrage: Evidence from the Volkswagen short squeeze
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional chronology; option strategy and constraints; price evidence; intraday evidence; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a vivid event only as the entry point and then reconstructs positions, margin constraints, fundamental value and trading behavior before interpreting inefficiency.
transfer_limit: The Volkswagen episode is exceptional and ex post institutional reconstruction does not transfer mechanically to routine mispricing settings.

title: The term structure of equity risk premia
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; equity-yield construction; dividend-futures data; expected-return estimates; liquidity and bounds; conclusion
teaching_function: Organizes the paper around a disputed term-structure fact and makes instrument construction, liquidity and no-arbitrage bounds part of the evidence chain.
transfer_limit: Dividend-strip samples are short and specialized; estimates should not be generalized to all horizons or historical regimes.

title: Market efficiency in the age of big data
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; high-dimensional learning model; in-sample prediction; out-of-sample prediction; pricing implications; conclusion
teaching_function: Connects investor learning and econometrician learning so that in-sample predictability, out-of-sample predictability and market efficiency are not rhetorically conflated.
transfer_limit: Its asymptotic learning environment does not validate a particular real-world trading strategy or machine-learning implementation.

title: Machine learning in the Chinese stock market
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data and methodology; out-of-sample results; variable importance; economic value; transaction costs and price limits; conclusion
teaching_function: Reports prediction separately for stocks and portfolios and keeps market-specific trading frictions in the main validation sequence.
transfer_limit: China-specific ownership, liquidity and daily price limits make the predictor ranking and implementability evidence nonportable.

title: A factor model for option returns
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; option-specific challenge; IPCA method; in-sample tests; out-of-sample tests; daily robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains why short-lived options require conditional loadings before introducing the latent-factor method and evaluating pricing performance.
transfer_limit: Latent IPCA factors improve fit but do not automatically supply an economic interpretation; option filters and return definitions remain consequential.

title: Size-adapted bond liquidity measures and their asset pricing implications
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; measurement problem; estimator construction; precision validation; asset-pricing applications; conclusion
teaching_function: Starts from trade-size-dependent measurement error and validates a revised liquidity measure before using it in pricing tests.
transfer_limit: The correction is tailored to bond trade-size distributions and cannot be imported unchanged into equity or dealer-quote settings.

title: Machine learning and fund characteristics help to select mutual funds with positive alpha
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; fund data; prediction targets; machine-learning methods; out-of-sample portfolios; net alpha; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines an investor-facing prediction target and evaluates whether fund selection produces net out-of-sample alpha rather than only classifier accuracy.
transfer_limit: Survivorship filters, characteristic availability, fees and model search limit any claim that the selected managers possess causal skill.

title: Mutual fund performance at long horizons
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; horizon mismatch; theoretical predictions; simulations; annual and decade outcomes; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows why monthly arithmetic alpha and long-horizon investor wealth answer different questions and derives the appropriate comparison before reporting results.
transfer_limit: Compound-return and benchmark choices are suitable for long-horizon wealth questions but do not replace monthly risk-adjusted evaluation in every application.

title: Empirical evaluation of overspecified asset pricing models
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; overspecification taxonomy; set estimation; testing restrictions; empirical evaluation; conclusion
teaching_function: Names the exact nonuniqueness problem created by overspecified SDFs and aligns the identified set, test and empirical object with that failure.
transfer_limit: The method addresses overspecification under its admissible-SDF framework and should not be presented as a remedy for every weak-identification problem.

title: Comparing factor models with price-impact costs
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; comparison criterion; price-impact model; empirical calibration; institutional scale; conclusion
teaching_function: Replaces frictionless Sharpe-ratio ranking with a utility comparison that internalizes price impact and makes investor scale part of model evaluation.
transfer_limit: Rankings depend on the price-impact specification, risk aversion and assets under management; they are not universal model rankings.

title: Machine learning from a “Universe” of signals: The role of feature engineering
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; real-time signal construction; methods; out-of-sample comparison; simple recursive benchmark; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a raw real-time signal universe and a simple benchmark to show that apparent machine-learning gains can come from feature curation rather than the algorithm.
transfer_limit: The conclusion concerns the tested signal libraries and implementations; it does not show that machine learning is generally inferior to simple rules.

title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; sample splitting; method comparison; out-of-sample evaluation; economic value; variable importance; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines return prediction as the common task across a broad method family and separates tuning, validation, statistical performance and portfolio value.
transfer_limit: Prediction improvements do not identify economic mechanisms and the 1957–2016 stock universe reflects a particular data and computing era.

title: The Rate of Return on Real Estate: Long-Run Micro-Level Evidence
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; return definitions; prior-measurement audit; archival data; income and total returns; asset-class benchmarks; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes measurement assumptions, expenses, income yields and holding returns visible before comparing real estate with other assets.
transfer_limit: Oxbridge endowment properties before 1983 are not representative of modern households, leveraged investors or all commercial real estate.

title: Production Networks and Stock Returns: The Role of Vertical Creative Destruction
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; network measure; stylized facts; model; calibration; mechanism tests; conclusion
teaching_function: Orders the paper as new return facts, a general-equilibrium mechanism, quantitative discipline and additional predictions rather than fitting a model before establishing the fact.
transfer_limit: The vertical-position measure and creative-destruction mechanism are production-network-specific and the calibration does not uniquely identify the model.

title: Π-CAPM: The Classical CAPM with Probability Weighting and Skewed Assets
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; primitives; equilibrium; pricing predictions; calibration; stock and option tests; conclusion
teaching_function: Adds one behavioral primitive to a familiar benchmark and maps each resulting prediction to a distinct empirical test.
transfer_limit: Probability weighting and the skewed-asset environment are specific primitives; successful predictions do not establish a unique behavioral explanation.
metadata_note: Local MinerU OCR renders the Greek Π in the title and formulas as 5; use the publisher title Π-CAPM.

title: Anomalies and False Rejections
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; multiple-testing framework; simulations; strategy universe; empirical application; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes selective reporting and the unseen strategy universe part of the estimand and evaluates alternative multiple-hypothesis controls in simulation before application.
transfer_limit: The inferred false-discovery proportion depends on a model of researchers’ unobserved signal draws.

title: Replicating Anomalies
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; common replication protocol; microcap controls; multiple-testing adjustment; category diagnostics; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses one transparent construction protocol to show how microcaps, weighting and multiplicity change the apparent anomaly inventory.
transfer_limit: Its encyclopedic length and 452-variable appendix are evidence infrastructure, not a prose-length template; replication choices remain contestable.

title: Comparing Cross-Section and Time-Series Factor Models
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; matched factor definitions; left-hand-side portfolios; model comparisons; conclusion
teaching_function: Creates a clean comparison by constructing cross-sectional analogues of familiar time-series factors and holding the test-asset question visible.
transfer_limit: The comparison is concentrated on Fama–French-style factors and selected anomaly portfolios and should not define all factor-model evaluation.

title: Testing Beta-Pricing Models Using Large Cross-Sections
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; asymptotic failure; estimator and specification test; extensions; empirical application; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains why the conventional estimator fails when N is large and T fixed before presenting the correction, extensions and changed empirical conclusion.
transfer_limit: The inference applies to a particular large-N fixed-T regime and is too specialized to serve as generic two-pass-regression prose.

title: Bond Risk Premiums with Machine Learning
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; research design; yield and macro forecasts; cross-maturity evidence; out-of-sample economic gains; interpretation; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates yield-only and macro-plus-yield forecasts and uses maturity-specific variable importance to connect prediction gains to macro-finance questions.
transfer_limit: Nonlinear forecasting evidence and correlations with risk-aversion proxies do not by themselves identify a structural bond-pricing channel.

title: Out-of-Sample Performance of Mutual Fund Predictors
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; predictor inclusion criteria; post-sample tests; panel evidence; arbitrage and competition; conclusion
teaching_function: Treats post-sample performance as a required validation object and investigates whether decay reflects original false discovery or changing competition.
transfer_limit: A decline after the original sample does not by itself prove that the initial relation was spurious or fully arbitraged away.

title: Thousands of Alpha Tests
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; false-discovery framework; observed and latent factors; missing data; in-sample and out-of-sample tests; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds a multiple-testing procedure around the actual alpha-estimation problem and keeps latent factors, missing data and out-of-sample behavior inside the validation design.
transfer_limit: The method is designed for thousands of correlated tests and should not become a ritual threshold for a small prespecified hypothesis set.

title: Comomentum: Inferring Arbitrage Activity from Return Correlations
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; proxy construction; arbitrage validation; reversal forecasts; simple model; additional predictions; conclusion
teaching_function: Introduces an indirect measure only after stating the model prediction and validates it against arbitrage activity before using it to forecast destabilizing effects.
transfer_limit: Comomentum is a proxy based on return correlations; its association with reversals is not direct causal evidence about arbitrageur trades.

title: Covered Interest Parity Arbitrage
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; rate measurement; implementable trades; institutional setting; dealer behavior; scalability; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows that a no-arbitrage claim begins with the funding rate actually available to traders and then distinguishes measured deviations from scalable profits.
transfer_limit: Conclusions depend on bank- and currency-specific funding access; headline CIP bases are not uniform arbitrage opportunities.

title: Narrative Asset Pricing: Interpretable Systematic Risk Factors from News Text
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; joint text-return model; regularization; pricing tests; out-of-sample tests; narrative interpretation; conclusion
teaching_function: Keeps factor construction, pricing performance and human interpretation as separate modules and retrieves source narratives after establishing statistical performance.
transfer_limit: Topic labels and retrieved narratives are model-dependent associations rather than identified causal economic shocks.

title: Option Return Predictability with Machine Learning and Big Data
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; nonlinear prediction problem; methods; out-of-sample performance; economic portfolios; information-friction and mispricing tests; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from an option-specific prediction question through method comparison and portfolio evidence before testing competing sources of predictability.
transfer_limit: Option filters, delta hedging and trading costs are consequential and predictive variables do not by themselves establish mispricing.

title: Unsmoothing Returns of Illiquid Funds
selected_sections: abstract; unheaded introduction; measurement failure; new unsmoothing method; hedge-fund application; real-estate application; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows how a measurement procedure mechanically changes estimated beta and alpha and validates it across two illiquid-fund settings.
transfer_limit: The moving-average return process and illiquidity assumptions are asset-class-specific; unsmoothed returns remain estimates rather than observed payoffs.
